A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Asymmetric Duos research, with readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. v1's full-results Appendix E is retained as Appendix G in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, uncertainty, selective-classification, ablation, model-soup, and throughput experiments in Section 5 and Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds direct deep-ensemble and Bayesian-method comparisons in Section 5.6 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains independently trained large and small models combined through two logit weights optimized for validation negative log likelihood. Revised training budgets and additional comparator implementations do not change the Duo algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet, ImageNet V2, Caltech 256, and in-distribution and out-of-distribution iWildCam classification. New comparisons use these existing datasets. Adding ConvNeXt results on iWildCam expands model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated pool-then-calibrate ResNet-50 deep ensembles with 2, 5, and 8 members, IVON with deterministic and sampled inference, and last-layer Laplace approximation (Tables 1–4). These substantive comparator families were not evaluated against Duos in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes iWildCam linear probing from 5 to 8 epochs, fine-tuning from 10 to 12 epochs, and Caltech fine-tuning from 20 to 16 epochs. Adaptive batch sizing becomes fixed sizes of 128 and 16. Soup construction changes from 32 candidates with 5 selected to 16 candidates with 3 selected. v2 also introduces base-model-controlled and FLOPs-controlled comparisons. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish their execution history.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of ensemble-size and computational-budget scaling, including allocating compute to stronger Duo base models, and examines IVON inference with 2–32 samples. The original unweighted and UQ-only ablations, entropy comparison, and temperature-weight analysis remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds tabular ± summaries and specifies 32 sampled ensemble subsets drawn from 10 independently trained ResNet-50 checkpoints (Appendix A.5). This does not mean 32 independent training runs. The new ± quantities are not explicitly defined; Figure 1's standard deviation across model choices already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 add substantial comparative results. For example, Table 1 reports accuracy of 81.87±0.19 for ResNet-50 plus EfficientNet-B2 versus 81.97±0.13 for five ResNet-50 ensemble members, at 27% versus 400% additional FLOPs. Numerous existing plots change, and Figure 14 gains ConvNeXt iWildCam results. Revised fine-tuning settings prevent treating affected scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The prediction, uncertainty, weighted-logit, and FLOPs-balance definitions remain substantively unchanged. A corrected closing parenthesis is typographical; neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claim that a small, appropriately weighted sidekick improves prediction and uncertainty with fractional additional computation. The new comparisons support this existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 attributes advantages over deep ensembles to architectural diversity and temperature aggregation, recommends choosing the strongest affordable base model, and discusses IVON compatibility and Laplace hardware constraints. Some new interpretations overreach: the claimed IVON advantage across all metrics contradicts Table 3, and Table 4 shows lower Laplace AUROC despite the prose claiming improvement.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, specifies NVIDIA L40S training hardware, documents ensemble checkpoint sources and construction, and describes the last-layer Kronecker-factored Laplace implementation. These extend the existing reproducibility documentation; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Laplace Redux and IVON references and positions Duos against these scalable Bayesian approaches. It also clarifies the distinction from Gontijo-Lopes et al. through fine-tuning paired models on the same data. Existing related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.6, Appendix A.5, comparison Appendices E–F, and a NeurIPS checklist, moving full results to Appendix G. Local wording, spelling, affiliation, and publication-header edits accompany these additions; the existing narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 introduces four multi-metric comparison tables and expands the ConvNeXt result grids from three to five dataset columns. Several plots have revised axes and legends. Figure 8 changes its plotted base-model label and correlation value while retaining an inconsistent caption and discussion.

improvement.justification: v1 presents Duos as a cheaper alternative to deep ensembles without directly benchmarking that alternative. v2 substantially closes this central evidential gap through calibrated comparisons controlling the base model and inference FLOPs (Tables 1–2), supplemented by Bayesian baselines and additional reproducibility information. Unsupported interpretations of Tables 3–4, undefined ± summaries, and stale Figure 8 text weaken reporting reliability, but do not outweigh the stronger evidence for the paper's central efficiency argument.
